## 4. Not verifiable here

Verified for real in this program: the page read back from the host by sha256 and byte count (`tools/readback.mjs`), and the CSP-wrapped local page driven by the real UI in Chromium (`tools/campaign_play.mjs`, `tools/uiscan.mjs`, smoke, tour, flow).

Not verifiable here, and said plainly in the final message:

- sound by ear: audio is checked by descriptors, cue tracing, decode and loudness classes, never by a listener;
- real GPU speed: frame costs are measured on SwiftShader (CPU-side costs only); the draw and triangle budgets are counts, not frame rates;
- hosted viewer behaviour: replaced by the user checklist below and the era-extended Diagnostics report;
- non-Chromium engines (Firefox, Safari) and real touch devices;
- human play of every mission: missions are played by scripted bots and a reference army, not by a person;
- the v8-save upgrade on the hosted origin: a staging artifact has another origin and an empty save, so the upgrade is proven locally by G5 (both-direction round trips) and by checklist item 1;
- that comedy, feel, set-piece quality, readability by eye, and the resemblance of silhouettes and palettes to real uniforms or franchises were judged by model panels and fresh agents, not by a person. Every such criterion is reported PANEL, never plain PASS.

User checklist (10 lines):

1. Open the link on the device that has the v8 save and check progress and stars.
2. The chooser opens with Continue on the last era.
3. An Ancient mission plays as before.
4. One mission per released era starts and its set-piece plays.
5. Sound plays after the first click.
6. Settings, Diagnostics, Copy, and paste it back (it carries the build stamp, registered eras, packs fetched, audio packs decoded, files fetched vs 404, decoded PCM MB).
7. Read five named lines aloud per era.
8. Settings: Reopen What's New and the gore setting.
9. Phone portrait Quick Battle.
10. Back keeps the era.
